title: Protocol for high-sensitivity western blot on murine hematopoietic stem cells
protocol: Euthanize mice with an approved method.
Pin euthanized mice to a dissection plate.
Sterilize surgical sites with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Dissect along dorsal and ventral midline and length of limbs to expose skeletal structures.
Clean and present bones for processing.
Mince bones using scissors in 2 mL cell isolation buffer.
Crush bone fragments by pestle and mortar for 3–4 rounds until bone fragments turn white.
Filter bone marrow cells with 40 μm cell strainers after standing for 5 minutes.
Sterilize the dissection areas and the external fur of the surgical sites with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Make a midline incision through the skin to expose the forelimbs, hindlimbs, ilium, pelvises, and vertebras.
Dislocate the tibias, femurs, humerus, pelvises, and vertebras in cold cell isolation buffer using curved forceps.
Wash the bones with 70% (v/v) ethanol for 3–5 seconds.
Transfer the washed bones into 2 mL of cold cell isolation buffer.
Remove muscle tissue from the bones using sterilized surgical instruments.
Mince the tibias, femurs, humerus, pelvises, and vertebrae into bone fragments.
Gently crush the bone fragments using a pestle and mortar with 2 mL of cold cell isolation buffer.
Transfer the supernatant to a 50 mL conical tube.
Re-suspend the bone fragments in 2 mL cold cell isolation buffer.
Repeat steps for mincing, crushing, transferring, and suspending until the bone fragments turn white.
Stand the 50 mL conical tube on ice for 5 minutes.
Carefully pipette the cell suspensions into a 15 mL conical tube passed through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Stand the 15 mL conical tube for 5 minutes to allow bone fragments to settle.
Carefully collect the supernatant containing bone marrow cells into a new 15 mL centrifuge tube, leaving 50–200 μL with the bone fragments in the original tube.
Remove the spinal cord from the vertebrae.
Crush the bone fragments instead of grinding to obtain higher cell viability.
Centrifuge the bone marrow suspension at 550 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and add 2 mL of ACK lysis buffer to the cell pellet.
Incubate the suspension for 2 minutes at 25°C–30°C to lyse any remaining red blood cells.
Add 10 mL cold cell isolation buffer to stop the lysis.
Filter the cell suspension into a 15 mL conical tube through a 40 μm filter strainer to remove cell clumps or debris.
Centrifuge the filtered cell suspension again at 550 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant carefully without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend bone marrow cells in 500 μL cold cell isolation buffer.
Count cell numbers for antibody staining using a Flow Cytometer Attune NxT (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Resuspend HSCs in cell isolation buffer at a concentration of 1 × 10^5 cells per μL.
Aliquot 500 μL cells into each 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 20 μL of lineage (PE-Cy5) antibody mix to each tube.
Add 10 μL of anti-Sca-1 (PE-Cy7), 10 μL of anti-c-Kit (APC), 10 μL of anti-CD48 (APC-Cy7), and 10 μL of anti-CD150 (PE) antibodies into each tube.
Incubate the tubes at 4°C on a shaker in the dark for 1 h.
Add 1 mL cell isolation buffer to each tube after staining.
Centrifuge them at 550 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the cells in cell isolation buffer to a final concentration of 5 × 10^7 cells per mL.
Store stained cells at 4°C in the dark before sorting.
Add 7-AAD at a final concentration of 0.5 μg/mL, detected in the PE-1 Cy5 channel, for 5 min.
Start the BD FACS Aria III sorter for a standard quality control setup.
Set the sorter nozzle to 70 μm with a sorting speed of 20,000–30,000 events per second.
Adjust sheath pressure to 70 psi and drop drive frequency (ddf) to 89 kHz.
Maintain threshold rate at 1/5–1/3 of ddf.
Set sort precision mode to Purity Precision Mode.
Transfer 1 mL cell suspension to a 5 mL Polystyrene tube.
Filter the cells immediately before sorting.
Turn on Sample Agitation to 100 g to prevent clumping.
Set the sample temperature inside the injection chamber to 4°C.
Use a 200 μL PCR tube as collection tube during sorting.
Coat the collection tube with FBS or BSA before adding cell isolation buffer.
Each collection tube can acquire up to 5×10^5 cells in 30 μL of collection buffer.
Set up the cell sorter according to manufacturer's instructions.
Number collection tubes from 1 to 5 and label them for receiving different numbers of HSCs (100, 500, 1,000, 5,000, and 10,000).
Sort bone marrow cells immediately after staining.
Use EPPENDORF PCR cooler 0.2 mL rack to keep samples cool during sorting.
Aliquot cell suspensions before filtering them for sorting.
Turn on the sample agitation mode if available on the sorter.
Manually resuspend cells if agitation mode is unavailable.
Reanalyze isolated HSCs using Attune NxT after sorting.
Spin down sorted HSCs in a PCR tube at 550 g for 5 min at 4°C without a break.
Gently remove the supernatant until approximately 4 μL of cell suspension remains.
Mix 4 μL of 2× lysis buffer with the sample.
Leave the mixture on ice for 10 minutes.
Lysate 10,000 cells with 8 μL of 1× lysis buffer.
Add 2 μL of 5× loading buffer to the cell lysate.
Heat the lysate on a heat block at 100°C for 3 minutes.
Incubate the sample with primary antibodies (1:1000 in Primary antibody dilution buffer) on a shaker at 4°C for 12–16 hours.
Wash the membrane 3 times.
Incubate the membrane with HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies for 1 hour at 25°C–30°C.
Use Western Chemiluminescent HRP Substrate for western blot detection.
